key_insight: Task-aware fusion of complementary structural encoders and intermediate layers improves materials-property prediction over a fixed representation bridge.
engineering_relevance: TCAF offers a more parameter-efficient bridge for materials language models, with reported gains in prediction quality and roughly half the overall training time of MatterChat.
method: Combine CHGNet features with intermediate Zatom-1 representations.
Use task-conditioned latent queries to select and fuse representations through attention.
Train the bridge directly on downstream prediction tasks without separate contrastive pretraining.
evidence_signal: Across classification and regression tasks, TCAF outperforms MatterChat with up to 47.8% lower RMSE; adding UMA-S yields the highest macro-average classification accuracy of 89.61%.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify dataset sizes or out-of-distribution tests, leaving generalization to unfamiliar materials uncertain.
paper_title: Choosing the Right Representations: Task-Aware Fusion for Multimodal Materials Language Models
